neighbours.label: the noun completing a set phrase of spending or losing time or life (lost their lives, spent years, save the day)
fire: Dozens of miners lost their lives when the shaft collapsed.
The committee spent months arguing over a single clause.
A late goal from the substitute helped save the day.
Many sailors lost their lives in the winter storms of 1913.
He has spent decades studying the migration of eels.
Volunteers spent weeks clearing the flooded houses.
Once again the quiet librarian managed to save the day.
Two climbers lost their lives on the north face last year.
quiet: Dozens of miners lost their helmets when the shaft collapsed.
The committee spent money arguing over a single clause.
A late goal from the substitute helped the team win.
Many sailors lost their cargo in the winter storms of 1913.
He has spent a fortune studying the migration of eels.
Volunteers spent their savings clearing the flooded houses.
Once again the quiet librarian managed to find the book.
Two climbers lost their ropes on the north face last year.

notes: Card: ' lives' x11, ' years' x5, ' day' x4, ' weeks' x3. Probe: 'lost their lives' 0.71, 'spent years' 0.62, 'save the day' 0.82, 'lost his keys' 0.08.
